evals.name: sponsor-intro-deck
evals.prompt: I'm meeting with a couple of engineers from a robotics company next month who might sponsor our lab. Can you make me a short PowerPoint (6-8 slides) that introduces the ATR Lab, explains our telepresence and Physical AI work, makes the case for sponsoring us, and ends with how to reach us? Save it as sponsor-intro.pptx.
evals.expected_output: A 6-8 slide .pptx built on the ATR presentation template layouts (Hazard Gold system): navy/gold palette, Source Sans 3, ATR logo + separate KSU academic wordmark (no athletic Flash logo), verified facts only with [placeholders] for unknowns, verified handles (@atrlab_kent, GitHub ATR-Lab) and no @atr_kent, speaker notes, alt text, no overflow.
expectations: sponsor-intro.pptx exists
Deck has 6-8 slides
Slides are built on ATR template layouts
No forbidden/incorrect facts (@atr_kent, wrong college, Room 236, old phone, wrong name)
Only brand fonts (or the Arial fallback) are used
Speaker notes on at least 75% of slides
Closing/contact uses the verified lab website
brand_check reports 0 errors
No athletic Flash logo or retired block logo
No fabricated or inflated claims (verified facts or visible placeholders only)
Visually on-brand and free of overflow/collisions (render reviewed)

evals.name: nasa-quad-chart
evals.prompt: We need a NASA quad chart for our new paper: 'Latency-Adaptive Haptic Feedback for Remote Manipulation' ([Author list]), IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2026, DOI 10.1109/LRA.2026.1234567. Background: remote operators lose grasp precision when round-trip delay goes above about 200 ms. Analysis: within-subjects study with 24 participants, three latency conditions (50, 250 and 500 ms), adaptive vs fixed haptic gain. Results: adaptive feedback cut grasp failures by 31% at 500 ms. Significance: it makes Earth-based teleoperation of lunar surface robots more practical. Funded by NASA grant 80NSSC26K1234 under the NASA EPSCoR program. Save it as haptics-quad.pptx.
evals.expected_output: A single-slide (or single main slide) quad chart following NASA GSFC guidance: headings exactly 'Background or Science Question', 'Analysis', 'Results', 'Significance', 'Acknowledgements'; Arial >= 14 pt; main text navy/blue; short citation + DOI under the title; the NASA acknowledgement sentence with grant number and program; a results figure with labelled axes and units (or a clearly marked figure placeholder); details in speaker notes; ATR/KSU branding.
expectations: haptics-quad.pptx exists
All five NASA headings appear verbatim
DOI 10.1109/LRA.2026.1234567 appears on the slide
NASA acknowledgement sentence with grant number and EPSCoR program
No explicit text size below 14 pt
Explicit fonts on the quad are Arial (NASA guidance)
Speaker notes present
No forbidden/incorrect facts
brand_check reports 0 errors
Results figure has labelled axes and units, with no invented data
Quad reads as a strong, well-filled communication piece

evals.name: k12-instagram-post
evals.prompt: Make an Instagram post announcing that registration is open for our middle school summer robotics workshop, June 14-18, 2027, 9am to 3pm on the Kent State campus. Registration link: [link]. I need the image (portrait format), the caption and the alt text.
evals.expected_output: A 1080x1350 PNG in the ATR brand (navy/gold, Source Sans 3, legible on a phone, safe zones), a caption in AP/KSU style (June 14-18, 9 a.m.-3 p.m., no Oxford comma, 'Kent State University' first reference), camel-case hashtags, correct Instagram handle (@atr_lab) or none rather than @atr_kent, no invented details, alt text provided, no photos of identifiable minors.
expectations: A PNG image was delivered
Image is 1080 x 1350 (Instagram portrait)
At least 70% of pixels are within the brand palette
Caption delivered
Alt text delivered (>= 80 characters)
Caption uses AP time style (a.m./p.m.)
No forbidden/incorrect facts (e.g. @atr_kent)
Any lab handle in the caption is the verified Instagram handle @atr_lab
Image text is accurate (no wrong handle, no invented details) and legible on a phone
Image is engaging and on-brand for a K-12 family audience

evals.name: flyer-brand-review
evals.prompt: A student made this flyer for our summer camp: eval-inputs/summer-camp-flyer-DRAFT.pptx. Can you check it for brand problems and fix it? Save the fixed version as summer-camp-flyer-FIXED.pptx and give me a list of what you changed.
evals.expected_output: Identifies most planted defects: athletic Flash logo, retired block ATR logo, white text on gold (contrast), off-palette gold, Comic Sans/Papyrus/Calibri fonts, gold text on white, 'KSU' in copy, 'College of Arts and Sciences', Oxford comma, '&', ordinals and time style, wrong contact (Room 236 / 330-672-9060), @atr_kent, wrong lab name 'Advanced Tele-Robotics Lab', tiny/low-contrast text, missing alt text. Produces a fixed flyer that uses the current ATR mark + KSU academic wordmark, brand fonts/colors and passes a brand check.
expectations: summer-camp-flyer-FIXED.pptx exists
Response identifies at least 10 of 14 planted defect categories
Fixed flyer contains no forbidden/incorrect facts
Fixed flyer uses only brand fonts (or Arial)
Fixed flyer has no Oxford comma and no '&' in copy
brand_check on the fixed flyer reports 0 errors
Fixed flyer has no athletic or retired logo
Fixed flyer is visually on-brand, legible and print-ready apart from flagged placeholders

evals.name: vendobot-paper-announcement
evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post and a short news blurb for the department website announcing our HRI 2026 paper on VendoBot. Keep it accurate, don't make up results.
evals.expected_output: Two pieces of copy that use the correct lab name on first reference ('Advanced Telerobotics Research Lab' at Kent State University), 'the lab' afterward, KSU/AP style (no Oxford comma, 'and' not '&'), no fabricated results/authors/quotes (bracketed placeholders instead), correct handles, plain-language framing, a CTA, and alt-text guidance if an image is suggested.
expectations: Both linkedin-post.md and news-blurb.md exist
Full lab name 'Advanced Telerobotics Research Lab' used
'Kent State University' named
No forbidden/incorrect facts
No '&' in the copy
HRI 2026 named
No 'KSU' abbreviation in running copy
No fabricated results, quotes or authors; claims match the public abstract
Kent State editorial style (no Oxford comma, 'the lab' after first reference, no 'Dr.' in news copy)
